title: Substrate Launch: the API for modular AI

summary: Rob Cheung presents Substrate publicly for the first time at the AI Engineer World's Fair, following a recent launch after approximately one year of private client work. His central thesis is that the best current AI products use multiple inference runs across different model types in logical structures rather than relying on a single foundation model. He positions modular intelligence as superior to monolithic intelligence because it produces systems that are inherently more legible, debuggable, extensible, and evaluable since decision trees become explicit and verifiable at each step. Substrate consists of two coupled components: a developer SDK that lets users describe computation graphs over any number of intelligence nodes spanning modalities like text generation, image generation, speech transcription, JSON, embeddings, and code execution, and an inference engine specifically built to run these computation graphs efficiently. The engine leverages a coordinated compute cluster enabling static and dynamic optimizations including batching, caching, networking concurrency, and physical placement. Cheung contrasts Substrate with typical frameworks that dispatch separate API calls, each incurring DNS resolution, proxy traversal, authentication, and load balancing overhead adding hundreds of milliseconds per step. Substrate instead transfers data between nodes at microsecond timescales, roughly 10,000 times faster, making online applications with dozens of nodes feasible. He also highlights investment in best-in-class JSON mode for reliability and speed, noting JSON decoding as one of the most useful patterns for multi-inference runs. The talk is constrained to five minutes, and he invites attendees to visit the Expo floor, scan a QR code for credits, or contact him via the website substrate.run.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Performance Advantages Over API Dispatch
